rubric_items.reason: Each of the six acceptance criteria maps to one or more REQs. AC5 is split into REQ-9 to REQ-12. The 'spot long-unseen patients' motivation is listed under Out of scope with a reason.
Almost all REQs are atomic and can be tested. REQ-13 also restates the baseline rule about the patient's own page, which adds a second behaviour outside the list.
Every known REQ cites a ticket line or a baseline section. REQ-4 is correctly marked assumed, with a real basis in the glossary definition of Completed. Nothing is invented.
The ticket does not clash with the baseline. AC6 and the data-protection rule agree. The hospital time zone is resolved from the baseline constraints without conflict.
Three questions, none blocking, each with real options and a sensible default. Product questions go to the product owner and the glossary question goes to the tech lead.
Plain and readable. The REQ-12 statement repeats a ticket fragment awkwardly, and claims C6 and C7 are declared but no requirement uses them.
